prompt: Users report that certain queries hang intermittently instead of returning: the query appears to stall indefinitely and never completes. The hang shows up only under some plans (notably ones involving a LIMIT) where the plan contains a Share Input Scan node, and it happens only some of the time. Investigate the root cause in the executor and propose a fix (which file/function(s) need to change and how).

answer_points: Root cause is in src/backend/executor/nodeShareInputScan.c: cross-slice shared-scan readers and the writer coordinate through a shared-memory hash table (shareinput_Xslice_hash) of per-share 'xslice state' entries

The entry is normally removed by whichever participant (reader or writer) references it last; if a reader is squelched (e.g. its Hash Join's inner side had no rows) before the writer even initializes, the reader can remove the entry first
When the writer later initializes, it finds no existing entry, creates a new one, and tries to communicate with readers that are already squelched and gone — so the writer hangs

Fix direction: disallow a reader from removing the xslice-state hash entry when it is squelching (e.g. release_shareinput_reference needs to know it's being called during a squelch, such as via a new bool parameter) so the writer can still find/use it
A finer-grained debug GUC (e.g. debug_shareinput_xslice) is a reasonable addition for diagnosing this class of issue
